items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: walked over to the side of the stage where Redd and Billy were behind a curtain and proceeded to chew Billy out.

ctx.x: Not with the band. Basie fired him, right then, gave him his ticket home and told him good-bye. He never did play a note, not with the band. He came in all hot, you know had his hat over to the side. It didn’t work like that. The band was a very well-oiled machine and it was a band, it was a big band, it was a full ensemble. Basie played the band like he played the piano. And it had to work like that. You couldn’t have 18 or 19 superstars up there ‘cause it never works. So the band was as a unit. And it had to be…

anybody that ran roughshod through the band. Basie wouldn’t stand for that. He just would not. And I never saw him get mad at anybody in the band except that one time. He was a very affable, easy going, wonderful man and just marvelous to work for, but you didn’t sass him, you did not sass him. One time we were playing a theater in LA and we were on stage, a big production thing, Oscar Peterson was there and Ella Fitzgerald and her trio. And so one night, let me see who was it? I think it was Redd Foxx and Billy…
Interesting. What — have you ever been on a gig when Joe Williams was a guest vocalist?
